nodes.label: tE mass-distance-velocity degeneracy
nodes.rationale: A microlensing timescale tE alone conflates the angular Einstein radius and the relative proper motion, so it can't separate a lens's mass from its distance without finite-source effects, parallax, or an independent proper motion measurement -- exactly why brown-dwarf-mass lenses are hard to identify/characterize from microlensing alone. The whole pipeline (model, priors, derived quantities) exists to make this degeneracy visible rather than hide it behind a single confident point estimate.

nodes.label: networkx
nodes.rationale: networkx appears in requirements.txt but is never mentioned or explained anywhere in CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, or README.md -- an unexplained dependency, possibly a stray package similar to the 'sandbox-only stray package' CHANGELOG session 3 describes hand-filtering out of a previous pip-freeze regeneration.

nodes.label: sympy
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md/CHANGELOG.md describe sympy as a one-time dev tool for derive_binary_quintic.py, explicitly 'not a project dependency' meant to stay scoped to scratch/ -- but requirements.txt (this file) lists sympy==1.14.0 directly, contradicting that stated convention. Flagged for review rather than silently reconciled.

nodes.label: Unresolved ~15deg alpha discrepancy vs Bond et al. 2004
nodes.norm_label: unresolved ~15deg alpha discrepancy vs bond et al. 2004
nodes.rationale: The current best validated 2L1S solution for O-03-BLG235 (chi2=1825.35, alpha~209.2deg, joint MCMC best sample tight-refined) is a genuine caustic crossing and scores better than Bond et al.'s own chi2 (1952.9), but its alpha is still ~15deg off Bond's published 223.8deg -- an open discrepancy not yet chased down.

nodes.label: Non-physical near-miss cusp solutions
nodes.rationale: Once the flux-calibration bug was fixed, chi2 minimization began favoring non-physical 'near-miss cusp' trajectories (no 3->5 image-count/caustic-crossing transition) that score numerically better than Bond et al.'s own published parameters. Only the image-count/caustic check catches these, not chi2 alone; 3 of 4 independent 2L1S searches (joint multi-start, both MOA-only searches) converged to such artifacts, blocking the planned BIC-vs-PSPL verdict.

nodes.label: MulensModel package
nodes.rationale: Used only as a one-time, trusted-oracle cross-check for the hand-rolled 2L1S implementation and later as an independent full-fit comparison (cross_check_mulensmodel_fit.py) -- deliberately kept out of requirements.txt as a pipeline dependency (scoped to scratch/, needs its own separate pip install) despite being the actual source of this project's raw photometry via download_data.py.

nodes.label: MulensModel alpha-convention cross-check bug
nodes.rationale: A first cross-check against MulensModel showed 1-6% (far-field) up to ~250x (near-caustic) disagreement with binary_magnification, which looked like a real physics bug. It was actually a coordinate-convention bug in the comparison script itself: MulensModel's own alpha convention is shifted 180deg from what was assumed, confirmed empirically rather than trusted from the docstring. Explicitly called out as the same category of failure as the u0 sign bug: a wrong-but-plausible result that superficially looks like the thing being tested for.

nodes.label: u0 mirror-image sign bug
nodes.rationale: PSPL's u0 only enters the model squared, so curve_fit can converge to the mirror-image (wrong-sign) solution from a bad initial guess. Hit for real when consolidating two MCMC scripts: one dataset's hardcoded u0 guess was silently reused for another, producing a wrong-sign, artificially tight posterior that still looked converged; chi2 didn't flag it. Lesson: per-dataset fit configuration (initial guesses) is not safe to treat as a shared constant.

nodes.label: O-03-BLG235 frozen PSPL flux-calibration bug
nodes.rationale: preprocess_binary_data.py's one-time PSPL-based flux calibration (fs_ogle/fb_ogle/fs_moa) was frozen and reused for every downstream fit including the 2L1S search. Evaluating chi2 at Bond et al. 2004's real published parameters gave 31,982 under the frozen calibration vs. 1,953 once fs/fb are re-solved analytically per trial against the true trajectory -- frozen values were off by 40%+, with fb_ogle even wrong-signed. This calibration bug, not a search-algorithm problem, was the real reason every 2L1S search kept landing in the wrong basin (session 4's initial conclusion was itself wrong).

nodes.label: MOA-2019-BLG-008 KMT error-bar underestimation
nodes.rationale: Raw KMTNet/pySIS mag_err column (median 0.006 mag) understates the real point-to-point scatter (~0.1-0.2 mag) by roughly 16-49x, confirmed model-independently via a flat-line baseline fit (chi2/dof=2441 with no lensing model at all). A known property of raw KMTNet pipeline photometry; every published microlensing analysis rescales error bars before fitting. This, not the physical model or search algorithm, is why fit_2l1s_moa19008.py's first run produced uniformly bad chi2/dof (~100-350) regardless of trial parameters.

nodes.label: Annual parallax + Student-t likelihood plan
nodes.rationale: The plain Gaussian PSPL model doesn't fit real data well (O-05-BLG086: chi2/dof=2.14, standardized-residual std=1.46, moderate excess kurtosis 1.23, largest residuals clustering in specific time windows rather than scattering randomly) -- consistent with unmodeled physics (parallax) plus a globally heavier-than-Gaussian error distribution rather than bad photometry or a small discrete-outlier population. Two changes planned to replace the model outright (no flag/toggle) across every PSPL-based fit: annual parallax (Gould 2004 geocentric piE_N/piE_E via astropy) built first, then a Student-t likelihood (scale and dof both free) built second, chosen over Huber/sigma-clipping specifically because the heavy tails look global rather than a small outlier population.
